subtopics: Documented examples of major contradictory scientific or health findings (e.g., coffee, eggs, alcohol, hormone replacement therapy, dietary fat) and how the scientific and media communities handled the conflicts
How systematic reviews and evidence-grading frameworks such as GRADE and Cochrane assess and report inconsistent or contradictory evidence across studies
Methodological guidance for researchers on detecting internal contradictions within a single source and resolving conflicts between sources during a literature review
How the replication crisis in psychology and biomedical science illustrates contradictory findings, and the leading explanations for why studies conflict
Best practices for hedging language and explicitly flagging source ambiguity, uncertainty, or conflicting evidence in academic and journalistic writing
